_example._help: Entries in "sites" tell the TV how to read one index page. Only host and item are required; everything else is optional and falls back to automatic reading. All selectors are CSS selectors. "item" matches every event row; the others are looked up INSIDE each row, except "section" (headings of date groups, anywhere on the page: the nearest one above the row is used). "host" also matches its subdomains. "zone" (optional, e.g. "UTC" or "Europe/London") is the time zone for times the page writes without a zone label; an entry may hold only "host" and "zone", and its rows are then read automatically. "habit" (optional) is what to do on this site's stream pages right after they load: copy the "Habit for recipes.json:" line from a What happened? report into "sites" as it is (tap x/y are fractions of the hidden browser, button counts from 1). A habit learned on the TV wins; the shipped one is used when there is none. Copy this object into "sites" and fill it in. "feed" (optional, instead of "item"): the site's own data file, read in place of drawing the page: {"url", "items" (dotted path to the events array, empty = the answer itself), "filter" (field: value, keep equal ones), "link" (event page, e.g. "/watch/{id}"), "title", "subtitle", "section", "start" / "end" (epoch ms; "startUnit": "s" for seconds; live between them), "live" (a field that says live)}. In url, link and filter values {path:N} is the list address's Nth path part (0 first, -1 last), {field.sub} an event field, {x|text} a fallback. If the file fails or has no events, the page is read as usual.
_example.title: h3.name
_example.subtitle: .organiser
